subject: Biotechnology
title: Liquid Biopsies
description: Learn Liquid Biopsies in one minute.

hook.text: A blood draw instead of surgery — liquid biopsies find tumor DNA circulating in the bloodstream.

buildup.text: Dying tumor cells release cell-free DNA into blood — ctDNA carries the same mutations as the solid tumor.

discovery.text: Guardant360 detects ctDNA mutations in a 20 mL blood sample — guiding therapy without an invasive biopsy.

twist.text: ctDNA from early-stage cancers is extremely rare — detecting it requires sensitivity below one mutant molecule in 10,000.

climax.text: Serial liquid biopsies track treatment response in real time — watching mutations rise or fall with each blood draw.

punchline.text: Find cancer in a drop of blood — liquid biopsies redefine diagnosis.

quiz.question: What is cell-free tumor DNA (ctDNA)?
options: Synthetic DNA injected to detect cancer
Fragments of tumor DNA released into the bloodstream by dying cancer cells
DNA from immune cells that have attacked the tumor

details.summary: Liquid biopsies detect cancer by analyzing circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, and exosomes in blood samples. They enable non-invasive cancer detection, treatment monitoring, and early relapse detection without surgical tissue sampling, revolutionizing cancer management.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional biopsies are invasive, painful, and cannot be repeated frequently. Liquid biopsies from a simple blood draw enable real-time cancer monitoring, detect minimal residual disease after treatment, and may eventually enable cancer screening
takeaways: Blood samples contain tumor DNA fragments shed by cancer cells
Liquid biopsies detect cancer mutations, monitor treatment, and find relapses early
They complement tissue biopsies with non-invasive longitudinal monitoring

faq.question: How is cancer DNA found in a blood sample?
faq.answer: Dying cancer cells release small DNA fragments into the bloodstream. Ultra-sensitive sequencing methods detect cancer-specific mutations in these fragments among the vast majority of normal DNA. Digital PCR and targeted sequencing panels can detect tumor DNA at frequencies below 0.01 percent.

faq.question: Can liquid biopsies detect cancer before symptoms appear?
faq.answer: Multi-cancer early detection tests like Galleri analyze methylation patterns in cell-free DNA to detect over 50 cancer types from a blood draw. Clinical trials show promise for detecting cancers at stages I and II. FDA approval for screening is pending validation in large prospective studies.
